title: Payton Pritchard talks Jaylen Brown trade, contract extension with Celtics
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Payton Pritchard is set for an expanded role with the Celtics after Jaylen Brown's trade to the 76ers.
Pritchard, Celtics' Sixth Man of the Year in 2024-25, averaged 17 points per game in the 2025-26 season.
Pritchard downplays contract extension talks, focusing on improving his game as his contract runs through 2027-28.

title: A Fall River 911 call said a man had killed his parents and had children hostage. It turned out to be a hoax.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A false 911 call claimed a man killed his parents and was holding children hostage in Fall River.
The hoax prompted Fall River police to deploy a perimeter and Emergency Services Unit to Stafford Road.
Police are investigating the origin of the hoax call and will hold the caller accountable for false reporting.

title: Police to increase patrols downtown amid safety concerns, neighborhood group says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston police will increase patrols downtown following a series of violent incidents and community safety concerns.
Key focus areas include Brewer Fountain Plaza, Winter Street, and parts of Downtown Crossing and Park Street.
Efforts to boost safety include enforcing city ordinances and addressing Boston Police Department staffing shortages.

title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd visited Boston for Fan Expo Boston and explored the city together.
The actors dined at La Royal Cambridge, a Peruvian restaurant, and visited Neptune Oyster in the North End.
They also stopped by The Green Dragon Pub, a historic Irish pub, and took selfies with Boston statues.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 from 2 to 7 p.m.
The event includes music, games, giveaways, and a special concert as a thank-you to Boston fans.
Brown, traded to the 76ers, played 10 seasons with the Celtics, earning five All-Star selections.

title: Patriots trade OL Caedan Wallace to Dolphins
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Patriots trade offensive lineman Caedan Wallace and 2029 seventh-round pick to Dolphins for 2028 sixth-round pick.
Wallace, drafted 68th overall in 2024, played 10 games for Patriots with limited playing time in 2025.
Patriots re-sign long snapper Niko Lalos and continue strengthening offensive line with recent draft picks.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife criticized paranormal investigator Chris Mac in comments under a Salem event announcement post on Facebook.
Rife's remarks included telling Mac to commit suicide, sparking backlash from Mac's supporters and other online users.
Rife and Elton Castee plan to display haunted items from the Warren Museum, including the Annabelle doll, in Salem on August 27.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots, including $14.5 million guaranteed, range up to $20 million.
Since joining the Patriots in 2021, Hunter Henry has made 259 catches and 26 touchdowns, solidifying his role in the offense.
The Patriots retain Henry as a key veteran to support quarterback Drake Maye, enhancing team stability and offensive reliability.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed her 2011 Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, causing significant damage.
Neither the driver nor her 88-year-old passenger were injured, but the store is closed for repairs.
Acton Police requested to suspend the woman's license and are investigating the incident.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will close for 75 days starting August 31 for a safety project.
The project involves installing an EMAS to safely stop aircraft overruns and is expected to finish by Thanksgiving.
Closure may cause flight delays and increase air traffic over nearby communities, particularly during bad weather.
